audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Jacob at the well, Rachel meeting, Laban recognition, Leah/Rachel exchange, love/service language, hated/unloved Leah, and first four sons' naming wordplays.

verses.restored: Jacob lifted his feet and went to the land of the sons of the east.

familiar.text: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came into the land of the people of the east.

notes.title: Lifted his feet
notes.body: A vivid idiom for setting out after the Bethel encounter.

modern.text: Jacob resumed his journey and came to the land of the people of the east.

original.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב רַגְלָ֑יו וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ אַ֥רְצָה בְנֵי קֶֽדֶם

verses.restored: He looked, and behold, a well in the field, and behold, three flocks of sheep lying beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks. The stone over the mouth of the well was large.

familiar.text: And he looked, and behold a well in the field...

modern.text: He looked and saw a well in the field, and near it lay three flocks of sheep, because the sheep were watered from this well. And a large stone covered the mouth of the well.

original.text: וַיַּ֞רְא וְהִנֵּ֧ה בְאֵ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֗ה וְהִנֵּה שָׁ֞ם שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עֶדְרֵי צֹאן֙ רֹבְצִ֣ים עָלֶ֔יהָ כִּ֚י מִן הַבְּאֵ֣ר הַהִ֔וא יַשְׁק֖וּ הָעֲדָרִ֑ים וְהָאֶ֥בֶן גְּדֹלָ֖ה עַל פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵֽר

verses.restored: When all the flocks were gathered there, they would roll the stone from the mouth of the well, water the sheep, and return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.

familiar.text: And thither were all the flocks gathered...

modern.text: When all the flocks had been gathered there, the shepherds would roll away the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would return the stone to its place over the mouth of the well.

original.text: וְנֶאֶסְפוּ שָׁ֣מָּה כָל הָעֲדָרִ֗ים וְגָלֲל֤וּ אֶת הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וְהִשְׁק֖וּ אֶת הַצֹּ֑אן וְהֵשִׁ֧יבוּ אֶת הָאֶ֛בֶן עַל פִּ֥י הַבְּאֵ֖ר לִמְקֹמָֽהּ

verses.restored: Jacob said to them, My brothers, where are you from? They said, We are from Haran.

familiar.text: And Jacob said unto them, My brethren, whence be ye?...

modern.text: “My brothers,” Jacob asked the shepherds, “where are you from?” “We are from Haran,” they answered.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָהֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב אַחַ֖י מֵאַ֣יִן אַתֶּ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מֵחָרָ֖ן אֲנָֽחְנוּ

verses.restored: He said to them, Do you know Laban son of Nahor? They said, We know him.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Know ye Laban the son of Nahor?...

modern.text: “Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor?” Jacob asked. “We know him,” they replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם הַיְדַעְתֶּ֖ם אֶת לָבָ֣ן בֶּן נָח֑וֹר וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יָדָֽעְנוּ

verses.restored: He said to them, Is there peace with him? They said, Peace. And look, Rachel his daughter is coming with the sheep.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Is he well? And they said, He is well...

modern.text: “Is he well?” Jacob inquired. “Yes,” they answered, “and here comes his daughter Rachel with his sheep.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָהֶ֖ם הֲשָׁל֣וֹם ל֑וֹ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ שָׁל֔וֹם וְהִנֵּה֙ רָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ בָּאָ֖ה עִם הַצֹּֽאן

verses.restored: He said, Look, the day is still great; it is not time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep and go pasture them.

familiar.text: And he said, Lo, it is yet high day...

modern.text: “Look,” said Jacob, “it is still broad daylight; it is not yet time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and take them back to pasture.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵ֥ן עוֹד֙ הַיּ֣וֹם גָּד֔וֹל לֹא עֵ֖ת הֵאָסֵ֣ף הַמִּקְנֶ֑ה הַשְׁק֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן וּלְכ֥וּ רְעֽוּ

verses.restored: They said, We cannot until all the flocks are gathered and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep.

familiar.text: And they said, We cannot, until all the flocks be gathered together...

modern.text: But they replied, “We cannot, until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone has been rolled away from the mouth of the well. Then we will water the sheep.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֮ לֹ֣א נוּכַל֒ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ כָּל הָ֣עֲדָרִ֔ים וְגָֽלֲלוּ֙ אֶת הָאֶ֔בֶן מֵעַ֖ל פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֑ר וְהִשְׁקִ֖ינוּ הַצֹּֽאן

verses.restored: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

familiar.text: And while he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep...

notes.title: Rachel shepherdess
notes.body: Rachel is introduced through active pastoral work.

modern.text: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

original.text: עוֹדֶ֖נּוּ מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֑ם וְרָחֵ֣ל בָּ֗אָה עִם הַצֹּאן֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔יהָ כִּ֥י רֹעָ֖ה הִֽוא

verses.restored: When Jacob saw Rachel daughter of Laban his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother, Jacob came near, rolled the stone from the mouth of the well, and watered the sheep of Laban his mother’s brother.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Jacob saw Rachel...

modern.text: As soon as Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, with Laban’s sheep, he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.

original.text: וַיְהִ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ רָאָ֨ה יַעֲקֹ֜ב אֶת רָחֵ֗ל בַּת לָבָן֙ אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֔וֹ וְאֶת צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֣י אִמּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֣שׁ יַעֲקֹ֗ב וַיָּ֤גֶל אֶת הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ מֵעַל֙ פִּ֣י הַבְּאֵ֔ר וַיַּ֕שְׁקְ אֶת צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Jacob kissed Rachel, lifted his voice, and wept.

familiar.text: And Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.

modern.text: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and wept aloud.

original.text: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ק יַעֲקֹ֖ב לְרָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ

verses.restored: Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s brother and that he was Rebekah’s son. She ran and told her father.

familiar.text: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's brother...

notes.title: Brother as kin
notes.body: Brother here means close male relative/kinsman.

modern.text: He told Rachel that he was Rebekah’s son, a relative of her father, and she ran and told her father.

original.text: וַיַּגֵּ֨ד יַעֲקֹ֜ב לְרָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י אֲחִ֤י אָבִ֨יהָ֙ ה֔וּא וְכִ֥י בֶן רִבְקָ֖ה ה֑וּא וַתָּ֖רָץ וַתַּגֵּ֥ד לְאָבִֽיהָ

verses.restored: When Laban heard the report of Jacob his sister’s son, he ran to meet him, embraced him, kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob recounted to Laban all these things.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Laban heard the tidings of Jacob...

modern.text: When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him all that had happened. Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ לָבָ֜ן אֶת שֵׁ֣מַע יַעֲקֹ֣ב בֶּן אֲחֹת֗וֹ וַיָּ֤רָץ לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיְחַבֶּק לוֹ֙ וַיְנַשֶּׁק ל֔וֹ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל בֵּית֑וֹ וַיְסַפֵּ֣ר לְלָבָ֔ן אֵ֥ת כָּל הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: Laban said to him, Surely you are my bone and my flesh. He stayed with him a month of days.

familiar.text: And Laban said to him, Surely thou art my bone and my flesh...

modern.text: Then Laban declared, “You are indeed my own flesh and blood.” After Jacob had stayed with him a month,

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לָבָ֔ן אַ֛ךְ עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב עִמּ֖וֹ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים

verses.restored: Laban said to Jacob, Because you are my brother, should you serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?

familiar.text: And Laban said unto Jacob, Because thou art my brother...

modern.text: Laban said to him, “Just because you are my relative, should you work for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב הֲכִי אָחִ֣י אַ֔תָּה וַעֲבַדְתַּ֖נִי חִנָּ֑ם הַגִּ֥ידָה לִּ֖י מַה מַּשְׂכֻּרְתֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: Now Laban had two daughters. The name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.

familiar.text: And Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah...

modern.text: Now Laban had two daughters; the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.

original.text: וּלְלָבָ֖ן שְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֑וֹת שֵׁ֤ם הַגְּדֹלָה֙ לֵאָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַקְּטַנָּ֖ה רָחֵֽל

verses.restored: Leah’s eyes were tender, but Rachel was beautiful in form and beautiful in appearance.

familiar.text: Leah was tender eyed; but Rachel was beautiful and well favoured.

notes.title: Tender eyes
notes.body: Rakot can mean tender, soft, delicate, or weak. The phrase is difficult and should not be flattened.

modern.text: Leah had weak eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.

original.text: וְעֵינֵ֥י לֵאָ֖ה רַכּ֑וֹת וְרָחֵל֙ הָֽיְתָ֔ה יְפַת תֹּ֖אַר וִיפַ֥ת מַרְאֶֽה

verses.restored: Jacob loved Rachel. He said, I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.

familiar.text: And Jacob loved Rachel; and said, I will serve thee seven years...

modern.text: Since Jacob loved Rachel, he answered, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”

original.text: וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת רָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶֽעֱבָדְךָ֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים בְּרָחֵ֥ל בִּתְּךָ֖ הַקְּטַנָּֽה

verses.restored: Laban said, Better that I give her to you than give her to another man. Stay with me.

familiar.text: And Laban said, It is better that I give her to thee...

modern.text: Laban replied, “Better that I give her to you than to another. Stay here with me.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֗ן ט֚וֹב תִּתִּ֣י אֹתָ֣הּ לָ֔ךְ מִתִּתִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ לְאִ֣ישׁ אַחֵ֑ר שְׁבָ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי

verses.restored: Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they were in his eyes like a few days because of his love for her.

familiar.text: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days...

modern.text: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.

original.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ד יַעֲקֹ֛ב בְּרָחֵ֖ל שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֑ים וַיִּהְי֤וּ בְעֵינָיו֙ כְּיָמִ֣ים אֲחָדִ֔ים בְּאַהֲבָת֖וֹ אֹתָֽהּ

verses.restored: Jacob said to Laban, Give me my woman, for my days are completed, and I will go in to her.

familiar.text: And Jacob said unto Laban, Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled...

modern.text: Finally Jacob said to Laban, “Grant me my wife, for my time is complete, and I want to sleep with her.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב אֶל לָבָן֙ הָבָ֣ה אֶת אִשְׁתִּ֔י כִּ֥י מָלְא֖וּ יָמָ֑י וְאָב֖וֹאָה אֵלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Laban gathered all the men of the place and made a feast.

familiar.text: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.

modern.text: So Laban invited all the men of that place and prepared a feast.

original.text: וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף לָבָ֛ן אֶת כָּל אַנְשֵׁ֥י הַמָּק֖וֹם וַיַּ֥עַשׂ מִשְׁתֶּֽה

verses.restored: In the evening he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter...

notes.title: Deceiver deceived
notes.body: Jacob, who deceived his father in darkness of sight, is deceived by Laban at night.

modern.text: But when evening came, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and he slept with her.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בָעֶ֔רֶב וַיִּקַּח֙ אֶת לֵאָ֣ה בִתּ֔וֹ וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתָ֖הּ אֵלָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֖א אֵלֶֽיהָ

verses.restored: Laban gave Zilpah his slave-woman to Leah his daughter as a slave-woman.

familiar.text: And Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid...

modern.text: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לָ֔הּ אֶת זִלְפָּ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לְלֵאָ֥ה בִתּ֖וֹ שִׁפְחָֽה

verses.restored: In the morning, look, it was Leah. He said to Laban, What is this you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah...

notes.title: What have you done?
notes.body: Jacob’s accusation mirrors the accountability formula used earlier in Genesis.

modern.text: When morning came, there was Leah! “What have you done to me?” Jacob said to Laban. “Wasn’t it for Rachel that I served you? Why have you deceived me?”

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּה הִ֖וא לֵאָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל לָבָ֗ן מַה זֹּאת֙ עָשִׂ֣יתָ לִּ֔י הֲלֹ֤א בְרָחֵל֙ עָבַ֣דְתִּי עִמָּ֔ךְ וְלָ֖מָּה רִמִּיתָֽנִי

verses.restored: Laban said, It is not done this way in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.

familiar.text: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country...

notes.title: Younger before firstborn
notes.body: Laban’s words sting Jacob’s own story: he, the younger, took the place of the firstborn.

modern.text: Laban replied, “It is not our custom here to give the younger daughter in marriage before the older.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן לֹא יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן בִּמְקוֹמֵ֑נוּ לָתֵ֥ת הַצְּעִירָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י הַבְּכִירָֽה

verses.restored: Complete the week of this one, and we will give you that one also for the service that you will serve with me yet another seven years.

familiar.text: Fulfil her week, and we will give thee this also...

modern.text: Finish this week’s celebration, and we will give you the younger one in return for another seven years of work.”

original.text: מַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וְנִתְּנָ֨ה לְךָ֜ גַּם אֶת זֹ֗את בַּעֲבֹדָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמָּדִ֔י ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת

verses.restored: Jacob did so and completed her week. Then he gave him Rachel his daughter as his woman.

familiar.text: And Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week...

modern.text: And Jacob did just that. He finished the week’s celebration, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ יַעֲקֹב֙ כֵּ֔ן וַיְמַלֵּ֖א שְׁבֻ֣עַ זֹ֑את וַיִּתֶּן ל֛וֹ אֶת רָחֵ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Laban gave Bilhah his slave-woman to Rachel his daughter as her slave-woman.

familiar.text: And Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid...

modern.text: Laban also gave his servant girl Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maidservant.

original.text: וַיִּתֵּ֤ן לָבָן֙ לְרָחֵ֣ל בִּתּ֔וֹ אֶת בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחָת֑וֹ לָ֖הּ לְשִׁפְחָֽה

verses.restored: He went in also to Rachel, and he loved Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet another seven years.

familiar.text: And he went in also unto Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah...

modern.text: Jacob slept with Rachel as well, and indeed, he loved Rachel more than Leah. So he worked for Laban another seven years. Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ גַּ֣ם אֶל רָחֵ֔ל וַיֶּאֱהַ֥ב גַּֽם אֶת רָחֵ֖ל מִלֵּאָ֑ה וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ד עִמּ֔וֹ ע֖וֹד שֶֽׁבַע שָׁנִ֥ים אֲחֵרֽוֹת

verses.restored: The Eternal saw that Leah was hated/unloved, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.

familiar.text: And when the LORD saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb...

notes.title: Hated/unloved
notes.body: Senuah can mean hated or unloved in comparison. The text centers Leah’s pain.

modern.text: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.

original.text: וַיַּ֤רְא יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי שְׂנוּאָ֣ה לֵאָ֔ה וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת רַחְמָ֑הּ וְרָחֵ֖ל עֲקָרָֽה

verses.restored: Leah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben, for she said, Because the Eternal has seen my affliction; surely now my man will love me.

familiar.text: And Leah conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Reuben...

notes.title: Reuben
notes.body: Reuben is linked with see, a son, and the Eternal seeing Leah’s affliction.

modern.text: And Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.”

original.text: וַתַּ֤הַר לֵאָה֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֔ן וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ רְאוּבֵ֑ן כִּ֣י אָֽמְרָ֗ה כִּֽי רָאָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ בְּעָנְיִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה יֶאֱהָבַ֥נִי אִישִֽׁי

verses.restored: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, Because the Eternal has heard that I am hated/unloved, he has given me this one also. She called his name Simeon.

familiar.text: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Because the LORD hath heard...

notes.title: Simeon
notes.body: Simeon is linked with hearing; the Eternal hears Leah’s pain.

modern.text: Again she conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son as well.” So she named him Simeon.

original.text: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר כִּֽי שָׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי שְׂנוּאָ֣ה אָנֹ֔כִי וַיִּתֶּן לִ֖י גַּם אֶת זֶ֑ה וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ שִׁמְעֽוֹן

verses.restored: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, Now this time my man will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons. Therefore his name was called Levi.

familiar.text: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me...

notes.title: Levi
notes.body: Levi is linked with being joined or attached.

modern.text: Once again Leah conceived and gave birth to a son, and she said, “Now at last my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” So he was named Levi.

original.text: וַתַּ֣הַר עוֹד֮ וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּן֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר עַתָּ֤ה הַפַּ֨עַם֙ יִלָּוֶ֤ה אִישִׁי֙ אֵלַ֔י כִּֽי יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים עַל כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא שְׁמ֖וֹ לֵוִֽי

verses.restored: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, This time I will praise the Eternal. Therefore she called his name Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

familiar.text: And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, Now will I praise the LORD...

modern.text: And once more she conceived and gave birth to a son and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” So she named him Judah. Then Leah stopped having children.

original.text: וַתַּ֨הַר ע֜וֹד וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֗ן וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַפַּ֨עַם֙ אוֹדֶ֣ה אֶת יְהוָ֔ה עַל כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד מִלֶּֽדֶת
